newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds slip as general caution continues.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds slip as general caution continues.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished lower Friday in thin trade as investors remained on the sidelines amid general market caution.

Traders and analysts said the market was still virtually devoid of investor flows with trade dominated by inter-bank activity. They said there still was a high level of uncertainty and that mood was seen gripping the market next week as well.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 fell $0.26 to 117.14, while Argentina's FRB due 2005 slipped 1/8 to 79-5/8.
"I expect high volatility next week, and I recommend caution and investors to reduce their portfolio duration," said Roberto Costa Bourdieu, senior fixed income analyst at Banco Rio de la Plata.

Another analyst said "the uncertainty continues, and because of that investors are staying away from the market. The main thing now is that the economic recovery continues and that the next official indicators are positive."
The domestic political situation has been complicated by recent corruption accusations by former Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo.

In addition to that, the weaker Mexican peso in recent weeks has players worried about an impact on Argentina's markets. Add to that rising concerns about Russia and some disquiet about the sustainability of the Dow Jones at its high levels and the result is a situation of investor hesitancy that could go on for some time.
"If something happens in Russia, it will hit all emerging markets," said Bourdieu.
At the same time, analysts point out there are good investment opportunities in Argentina considering the underperformance of Argentine bonds compared with most Latin American markets this year.
In the money markets, call money rates fell to 6.75 percent from 7.05 percent.
